[@magisk-install]Magisk – systemless root needs an unlocked bootloader; patches the ramdisk, not /system
Paper claimSec. 8 →

modern rooting is systemless, patching the partition image that holds the ramdisk (and the init it carries) rather than /system, and still requires an unlocked bootloader to reflash that image, so it still forfeits the verified-boot state and hardware-backed verdicts. (Which partition holds the ramdisk varies by device – boot, init_boot on Android 13+, or vendor_boot/recovery – but it is never /system; the Magisk docs phrase it as "the partition image that contains the ramdisk".)

"Your device's bootloader has to be unlocked" / "you need to patch the partition image that contains the ramdisk".

[@magisk-details]Magisk – patched init runs first and shapes the SELinux policy it then runs under
Paper claimSec. 8 →

modern root is control of init: the patched init runs before the SELinux policy is loaded (init loads it in userspace via security_load_policy, which magiskinit LD_PRELOAD-hooks), so the installer authors the policy its own daemon runs under (an unconstrained, permissive domain) rather than being confined by it – an administrative-tier initramfs modification, not an enlargement of in-system root.

"magiskinit replaces init as the first program to run." / "Sets LD_PRELOAD (init-ld) on init to hook security_load_policy" / "An unconstrained, permissive domain that magiskd and all root shells run in."

topjohnwuMagisk DocumentationMagisk Documentation: Internal Details · retrieved 2026-10-31

Paper claimSec. 8 →

leaving /system byte-identical keeps official OTAs applicable (not blocked as a modified /system would be); an OTA overwrites boot/init_boot, so root does not survive it automatically – Magisk is restored to stock before the OTA and re-installed to the updated slot after.

"Magisk does not modify read-only partitions by default, which makes applying official OTAs much simpler." / "When an OTA is available, first go to (Magisk app -> Uninstall -> Restore Images)." / "Go to the Magisk app and select (Install -> Install to Inactive Slot (After OTA)) to install Magisk to the updated slot."

[@aosp-dm-verity]AOSP dm-verity – editing /system fails verification (why systemless)
Paper claimSec. 8 →

dm-verity is the integrity mechanism protecting /system (a hashtree); verified boot covers /system and boot/init_boot alike, so neither is editable on a locked device. dm-verity plus read-only EROFS/super make /system a harder, read-only target than the single flashable boot image – a secondary reason the method patches boot, not because boot is unprotected.

"The ability to modify any of the blocks would be equivalent to breaking the cryptographic hash." / "If verification fails, the device generates an I/O error indicating the block can't be read." / "It appears as if the filesystem has been corrupted, as is expected."

[@rfc9334-rats]RATS architecture – Attester proves, Relying Party depends (direction of trust)
Paper claimSec. 8 →

remote attestation is a relying-party protocol; the device is the Attester that must produce evidence, a Verifier appraises it, and the Relying Party (app, service, or platform) is the party that depends on the result, so the guarantee runs to the relying party, not the owner.

Attester "A role performed by an entity (typically a device) whose Evidence must be appraised in order to infer the extent to which the Attester is considered trustworthy, such as when deciding whether it is authorized to perform some operation."

Relying Party "A role performed by an entity that depends on the validity of information about an Attester for purposes of reliably applying application-specific actions."
